title: Pickle-free models docs: SHAP explainer artifacts stay pickle-based and are not pickle-free even when the nested model is
answers: Is a SHAP explainer saved with MLflow pickle-free or safe to load from untrusted sources?
Why does MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false not stop loading a SHAP explainer everywhere?
Can I use skops trusted types to make a SHAP explainer pickle-free?
Where is the pickle-free models guide content about SHAP?
body:
Path: the pickle-free models guide (docs/docs/classic-ml/tracking/pickle-free-models/index.mdx) and the SHAP API docstrings for mlflow.shap.log_explainer, save_explainer and load_explainer (mlflow/shap/__init__.py) describe what is and is not pickle-free for SHAP artifacts.
Rule: SHAP explainer state is always pickle-serialized, regardless of serialize_model_using_mlflow. Even with the nested sklearn model in cloudpickle, the complete artifact is not pickle-free. Do not describe it as pickle-free, and do not offer skops trust lists as a way to make it safe. Standalone mlflow.sklearn models still use skops by default and can accept reviewed skops_trusted_types.
Symptom: Users assumed SHAP artifacts were pickle-free like standalone sklearn models, so they expected skops trust settings or MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false to make them safe to load.
Constraints: MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false blocks loading SHAP explainers outside Databricks Runtime and Databricks Model Serving. Inside those environments it does not block loading. load_explainer carries a warning to load only trusted sources.
applies: Use when documenting, answering questions about, or changing the pickle or safety guarantees of SHAP explainer artifacts versus standalone sklearn models.
says: The documentation incorrectly implies that model explanation artifacts are safe from untrusted code execution.
Disabling pickle deserialization does not block loading model explainers in managed serving environments.
Configuring trusted types does not make saved model explainer artifacts pickle free.
Warn users that model explainers remain serialized with pickle even when nested models are not.
Explain why model explanation artifacts cannot guarantee safe deserialization from untrusted sources.
search: Documentation and docstrings in docs/docs/classic-ml/tracking/pickle-free-models/index.mdx and mlflow/shap/__init__.py must not describe SHAP explainer artifacts as pickle-free because explainer state is always pickle-serialized regardless of serialize_model_using_mlflow. Skops trust lists cannot be offered to secure SHAP explainers, even when nested sklearn models use cloudpickle, whereas standalone mlflow.sklearn models continue to use skops by default with skops_trusted_types. Setting MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false blocks loading SHAP explainers outside Databricks Runtime and Databricks Model Serving, but does not block loading inside those environments, and load_explainer warns to load only trusted sources.
